q: A risk assessment identifies a threat with high impact but very low likelihood. Mitigating it would cost substantially more than the expected loss. Which risk response is MOST appropriate?
c: Accept the risk and document the decision
Transfer the risk through insurance
Mitigate the risk regardless of cost
Ignore the risk since likelihood is low

q: A development team is threat modeling a new payment service and wants a structured way to enumerate potential threats against each element of the data-flow diagram. Which approach BEST supports this goal?
c: Apply STRIDE categories to each data-flow element
Score each known vulnerability using CVSS
Commission an external penetration test
Review the enterprise risk register entries

q: An internal document states that all company laptops MUST use AES-256 full-disk encryption. Compliance is mandatory and no exceptions are listed. Which type of document is this?
c: A security standard
A security policy
A security guideline
A security procedure

q: During an internal audit, a CISSP-certified analyst discovers that a colleague has been falsifying vulnerability scan results to hide missed remediation deadlines. What should the analyst do FIRST?
c: Confront the colleague privately and ask them to stop
Report the findings through the organization's internal channels
File an ethics complaint with ISC2 against the colleague
Escalate directly to the external audit committee

q: A US-based SaaS provider hosts and processes EU customer personal data strictly on the instructions of its European business clients. Under the GDPR, how is the provider classified?
c: As a data processor
As a data controller
As a data subject
As a supervisory authority

q: An organization is beginning its business continuity program. Management wants to know which business processes and systems must be recovered first after a disruption. Which activity provides this answer?
c: A quantitative risk assessment
A disaster recovery test
A business impact analysis
A threat and vulnerability assessment

q: A manufacturer learns that a vulnerable open-source library may be embedded in firmware delivered by several of its third-party suppliers. Which practice gives the organization the BEST visibility into this exposure?
c: Signing non-disclosure agreements with every supplier
Increasing the frequency of internal code reviews
Purchasing cyber insurance covering supply chain incidents
Requiring a software bill of materials from each supplier

q: An online contract platform must ensure that a customer who electronically signs an agreement cannot later credibly deny having signed it. Which security concept is the platform enforcing, and what typically provides it?
c: Authenticity, provided by validating the customer's login credentials
Nonrepudiation, provided by digital signatures over the agreement
Integrity, provided by hashing the agreement after signature
Accountability, provided by recording the signing in an audit log

q: A data center asset valued at $400,000 has an exposure factor of 25% for a flood that historical records show occurs about once every 10 years. What annualized loss expectancy (ALE) should the risk analyst report for this threat?

After purchasing a cyber insurance policy covering ransomware losses, a CFO tells the board that the ransomware risk 'is now the insurer's problem.' What should the CISO clarify about this risk treatment?
c: The risk has been avoided, so the organization no longer needs ransomware-specific controls
Part of the financial impact is transferred, but accountability and uninsured impacts such as reputational damage remain with the organization
The risk has been fully mitigated because insurance operates as a compensating control
The risk has been accepted, because a premium was knowingly paid in place of deploying controls

q: Ahead of an acquisition, a security director commissions research into the target company's breach history, audits its control environment, and reviews its outstanding regulatory findings before integration begins. Which principle is the director demonstrating?
c: Due diligence
Due care
The prudent person rule
Compliance management

q: A CISSP consultant discovers that a client's water-treatment control system has a safety flaw that could endanger the public. The client, who pays the consultant's fees, instructs them to omit the finding and tell no one. Under the ISC2 Code of Ethics, why can the consultant not simply comply?
c: The canon to advance and protect the profession forbids concealing findings from fellow practitioners
The canon to act honorably requires the consultant to resign the engagement immediately
The duty of diligent and competent service to principals requires disclosure directly to the client's regulator
The canons are applied in priority order, and protecting society and the public trust outweighs duties owed to the client

q: A multinational plans to consolidate all HR records into a single cloud region in the United States. Counsel warns that several countries where employees reside have data localization statutes. What is the MOST significant risk-management implication for the consolidation plan?
c: The plan automatically violates GDPR because HR records are special-category personal data
Some employee records may be legally required to remain in-country, so the design must support per-jurisdiction storage or lawful transfer mechanisms
Under the cloud shared responsibility model, cross-border compliance obligations shift to the provider hosting the data
Encrypting the records in transit and at rest satisfies localization requirements because plaintext never leaves the country

q: An employee's suspected data theft could lead either to termination under HR policy or to criminal prosecution. The CISO asks why the investigation approach must be decided early. What is the BEST answer?
c: Criminal cases use the preponderance-of-evidence standard, so less rigorous collection is generally acceptable
Administrative investigations require law enforcement involvement from the outset
A criminal case demands proof beyond a reasonable doubt, so evidence handling must meet the strictest standard from the outset
Civil and criminal matters cannot arise from the same underlying incident, so a single path must be chosen now

q: A financial regulator opens an inquiry and formally demands five years of transaction logs. The operations team notes that the retention policy requires only three years, though older logs still exist on backup tapes. What should the organization do FIRST?
c: Issue a legal hold suspending routine destruction of all potentially responsive records, including the tapes
Destroy the logs older than three years because the retention policy authorizes their disposal
Produce only the three years of logs the policy requires, since the policy defines the legal obligation
Negotiate the scope of the demand with the regulator before preserving anything

q: A newly hired business continuity manager is launching the organization's first formal continuity program. Which element is MOST critical to obtain before any other work begins?
c: A completed inventory of the organization's critical business processes
Signed contracts with an alternate processing site provider
A tested disaster recovery plan for the primary data center
Documented senior management commitment and a chartered scope for the program

q: A BIA sets the maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) for the order-processing system at 24 hours. The DR team proposes a significantly cheaper recovery solution with a recovery time objective (RTO) of 30 hours. How should the continuity manager respond?
c: Accept the proposal, because RTO measures data loss while MTD measures downtime
Reject it, because an RTO longer than the MTD means unacceptable harm occurs before recovery completes
Accept it, provided the recovery point objective stays under 24 hours
Reject it, and set the RTO exactly equal to the MTD so no recovery budget is wasted

q: An accounts-payable clerk has not taken a vacation in three years and resists all cross-training. Internal audit suspects the clerk may be concealing fraudulent transactions that require daily maintenance. Which personnel security control is designed to surface this kind of scheme?
c: Separation of duties
Least privilege
Mandatory vacations
Nondisclosure agreements

q: An organization is about to notify a systems administrator of involuntary termination. The administrator holds privileged credentials across production systems. From a personnel security standpoint, when should the administrator's access be revoked?
c: At or immediately before the moment of notification, coordinated between HR and IT
At the end of the administrator's final scheduled shift, to allow for knowledge transfer
After the exit interview concludes and all company equipment has been returned
Within 24 hours of notification, per the standard deprovisioning service levels

q: After a risk assessment, a hospital cancels a pilot program that would have let clinicians access patient records from personal phones, because the exposure cannot be reduced to an acceptable level. Which risk response does this decision represent?
c: Risk transference
Risk mitigation
Risk acceptance
Risk avoidance

q: A CISO must present emerging AI-related threats to the board next week. No credible loss history or actuarial data exists for these threats, but the board wants the risks ranked to guide funding decisions. Which analysis approach is MOST appropriate?
c: Quantitative analysis, because board funding decisions require monetary ALE figures
Qualitative analysis using expert judgment to rate likelihood and impact on defined scales
Deferring the analysis until enough incident data accumulates to compute reliable annualized rates
A Monte Carlo simulation seeded with published industry breach-cost averages

q: A security architect wants a threat-modeling methodology that begins from business objectives and impact, connects technical threats to business risk through seven defined stages, and produces output executives can use to prioritize spending. Which methodology BEST fits?
c: STRIDE
DREAD
PASTA
VAST

q: During threat modeling, an analyst breaks an application into its components to identify trust boundaries, data flow paths, input points, and privileged operations before any threats are enumerated. What is this activity called?
c: Reduction analysis
Root cause analysis
Attack tree construction
Gap analysis

q: An organization is negotiating with a SaaS vendor that will process regulated customer data. The vendor offers its marketing security whitepaper as evidence of strong controls. Which contract provision gives the organization the STRONGEST ongoing assurance about the vendor's control environment?
c: A confidentiality clause obligating the vendor to protect customer data from disclosure
A service level agreement guaranteeing 99.9% platform availability
An indemnification clause covering losses arising from a vendor breach
A right-to-audit clause with an obligation to furnish independent assessments such as SOC 2 Type II reports

q: A defense contractor discovers that network interface cards bought through a discount broker may be counterfeit and carry unknown firmware. Beyond replacing the suspect cards, which change MOST directly addresses the root supply chain failure?
c: Requiring firmware integrity scanning of all devices at deployment time
Procuring only through authorized distributors with a verifiable chain of provenance from the original manufacturer
Adding the broker to the vendor risk register and raising its assigned risk rating
Imaging and penetration-testing a sample of every future hardware lot before deployment

q: A year after launching a security awareness program, the CISO must show the board whether the program is actually working. Which measure BEST demonstrates the program's effectiveness?
c: The percentage of employees who completed the annual training module
Average scores on the knowledge quiz taken immediately after training
The trend in employee click and reporting rates across periodic simulated phishing campaigns
The number of awareness posters, newsletters, and events delivered during the year

q: A security program includes short monthly videos reminding all staff to lock screens and report suspicious email, role-based courses teaching administrators secure configuration skills, and tuition support for security degrees. What distinguishes the monthly videos from the other two components?
c: They are awareness activities meant to keep security present in everyone's mind rather than to build job-specific skills
They are training, because they teach staff how to perform specific security tasks
They are education, because they build long-term security understanding across the workforce
They are social engineering exercises that test staff behavior rather than inform it

q: A utility is defining protection goals for the SCADA system that manages a regional power grid; customer billing runs on a separate platform. When tailoring the CIA triad for the SCADA environment, which emphasis is MOST appropriate?
c: Confidentiality first, because leaked grid telemetry would help attackers plan intrusions
Equal weighting of confidentiality, integrity, and availability, since the triad requires balance
Confidentiality and nonrepudiation, so that operator commands remain provable afterward
Availability and integrity first, because the grid must keep operating and its control data must be trustworthy

q: After a major breach, the board asks who bears ultimate accountability for the organization's information security program. What is the BEST answer?
c: The chief information security officer, as the designated security executive
Senior management and the board, who own enterprise risk and answer for the organization's direction
The IT department, which implements and operates the technical controls
Each data owner, since accountability follows ownership of the affected assets

q: A global firm's monitoring policy requires recording all employee chat messages. Counsel in a newly entered country advises that such recording violates that country's employee privacy law, but security leadership insists the policy must apply uniformly. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Apply the policy uniformly, since internal policy takes precedence inside a private company
Obtain blanket employee consent forms so the recording can lawfully continue
Comply with the local law and adapt the policy for that jurisdiction, documenting the exception through governance channels
Suspend all monitoring worldwide until the policy and every country's laws are harmonized

q: A business unit cannot meet the corporate encryption standard on a legacy platform scheduled for retirement in 18 months, and remediation would cost more than the platform's remaining value. What is the BEST way to handle the noncompliance?
c: Grant a formal, time-bound exception approved by the risk owner, with compensating controls and a review date
Rewrite the standard so that legacy platforms of this type fall outside its scope
Reclassify the platform's data at a lower sensitivity level so the standard no longer applies
Leave the standard unmet but undocumented, since the retirement date makes the issue self-resolving

q: A regulation requires unique user authentication on a hospital's clinical system, but the vendor's software supports only a shared login and cannot be modified. The system is essential to patient care. Which approach BEST reflects sound risk management?
c: Accept the risk, since the requirement is technically impossible to satisfy on this product
Remove the system from service until the vendor adds support for unique logins
Declare the regulation inapplicable because the vendor, not the hospital, controls the software design
Apply documented compensating controls, such as individual OS-level authentication and monitored access logs, that meet the requirement's intent

q: A beverage company's competitive advantage rests on a formula it has kept secret for decades through NDAs and restricted access. An executive proposes patenting the formula for stronger protection. What is the MOST important trade-off to explain to the executive?
c: Patents protect expressions of ideas, so the formula would need copyright protection instead
Patenting requires public disclosure and expires after a set term, while a trade secret can last indefinitely if secrecy is maintained
Trademark registration would protect the formula while still keeping it entirely secret
Trade secrets become enforceable only after formal registration of the secret with a government office

q: The board of directors publishes a statement that the organization will pursue aggressive digital growth while accepting only minimal risk to regulatory compliance. A product manager then asks the risk team how much deviation from the approved risk level is acceptable for her specific product line before escalation is required. Which concept BEST describes what the product manager is asking about?
c: Risk appetite
Risk capacity
Risk tolerance
Residual risk

q: A risk analyst is instructed to evaluate the exposure of a new payment platform under the assumption that no safeguards or countermeasures are in place, so leadership can understand the worst-case exposure before selecting controls. Which value is the analyst calculating?
c: Inherent risk
Residual risk
Secondary risk
Acceptable risk

q: An enterprise risk register lists the CISO as the owner of every one of its 45 entries, including risks to manufacturing uptime, financial reporting accuracy, and third-party logistics. A maturity assessment flags this arrangement as a weakness. What is the BEST recommendation?
c: Retain the CISO as owner of all entries because the security function has the deepest expertise in evaluating and treating risk
Reassign each risk to the manager accountable for the affected business process, with the security team acting as an advisor
Transfer ownership of the register to internal audit so that risk decisions are overseen by an independent function
Assign ownership of all entries collectively to the enterprise risk committee so treatment decisions are made by consensus

q: A CISO wants a forward-looking metric that will warn leadership when the organization's backlog of unremediated critical vulnerabilities is trending toward a level that could breach the board's stated risk thresholds, so treatment can begin before an incident occurs. Which type of metric BEST fits this need?
c: A key performance indicator
A key goal indicator
A return on security investment calculation
A key risk indicator

q: An organization posts prominent signs stating that all warehouse areas are under continuous video surveillance and that violators will be prosecuted. The signs are intended to discourage theft before it is attempted. From a functional perspective, what type of control are the signs?
c: Deterrent
Preventive
Detective
Corrective

q: To reduce ransomware exposure, an organization deploys fully automated same-day patching to all production servers. Two weeks later, an untested vendor patch takes the order-processing cluster offline for a full business day. From a risk management perspective, the outage exposure created by the new patching process is BEST described as what?
c: Residual risk
Control risk
Secondary risk
Inherent risk

q: A database administrator legitimately holds the schema-modification rights required for the role, but can also open and read the plaintext contents of executive compensation tables that the job never requires the administrator to view. Which security principle is MOST directly violated?
c: Least privilege
Need to know
Separation of duties
Dual control

q: An attacker bypasses an organization's perimeter firewall through a misconfigured rule, but the intrusion is contained because network segmentation, host hardening, and egress monitoring each independently limited what the attacker could reach. Which security design principle does this outcome illustrate?
c: Defense in depth
Zero trust
Security through obscurity
Fail-safe defaults

q: A newly appointed CISO discovers that security initiatives have been selected informally by IT engineers based on technical interest, and an external review notes that security spending shows no connection to the company's strategic objectives. Which action would BEST address the root cause?
c: Pursue ISO/IEC 27001 certification to demonstrate that a formal security program exists
Procure an integrated GRC platform to centralize the tracking of all security initiatives
Request an increased security budget so that more strategically relevant projects can be funded
Charter a cross-functional security steering committee to prioritize initiatives against business objectives

q: For three consecutive years, an organization's risk assessments identified an unsupported internet-facing server as a critical exposure, yet leadership declined to fund remediation each time. After a breach through that server, plaintiffs argue that executives were negligent. The executives' failure is BEST characterized as an absence of what?
c: Due diligence
Due process
Due care
The prudent man rule

q: A U.S.-headquartered manufacturer plans to ship network appliances containing strong cryptographic modules to a new engineering office abroad and to give developers there source-code access to the cryptographic libraries. Which legal issue MOST directly constrains this plan?
c: Cross-border personal data transfer rules that require approved contractual safeguards
Export control regimes that restrict transferring cryptographic hardware and source code across borders
Data localization statutes that require citizens' records to remain stored in their home country
Import tariff and customs valuation requirements imposed by the destination country

q: A company discovers that a competitor is marketing services under a nearly identical logo and brand name, causing several customers to sign contracts with the wrong firm. Which form of intellectual property protection MOST directly applies to this situation?
c: Copyright
Patent
Trade secret
Trademark

q: A SaaS provider confirms that personal data belonging to customers residing in several countries was exfiltrated, and containment is complete. Notification deadlines, thresholds, and required recipients differ across the affected jurisdictions. What should incident response leadership do FIRST regarding external disclosure?
c: Notify every affected individual worldwide within 72 hours of confirming the breach
Engage legal counsel to map each affected jurisdiction's notification obligations, deadlines, and required content
Defer all external notification until the forensic root-cause analysis is fully complete
Notify the data protection regulator in the country where the provider is headquartered

q: An organization files a lawsuit against a former contractor seeking monetary damages for misappropriating proprietary data. The security team asks what standard the collected evidence must ultimately satisfy for the organization to prevail in this proceeding. Which standard of proof applies?
c: Beyond a reasonable doubt
Clear and convincing evidence
Probable cause
Preponderance of the evidence

q: After detecting repeated probing from a specific source, a security team stands up a honeypot stocked with realistic decoy data along the intruder's existing attack path. The intruder breaks in, and the recorded activity supports prosecution. The defense argues the evidence should be excluded because the team lured the attacker. Which principle BEST supports admissibility?
c: Entrapment, because the honeypot induced an intrusion the attacker would not otherwise have attempted
Enticement, because the intruder had already demonstrated intent to attack before encountering the decoy
Exigent circumstances, because the evidence would have been destroyed without immediate collection
The plain view doctrine, because the intruder's activity was openly visible to monitoring tools

q: During an annual governance review, a CISO finds that the draft enterprise data protection policy mandates AES-256 for data at rest and names a specific vendor's full-disk encryption product for all laptops. What is the BEST recommendation for the CISO to make about this draft?
c: Approve the draft as written, because naming exact technologies makes enforcement measurable and audits simpler
Move the technology mandates into a supporting standard and keep the policy as a high-level statement of intent
Reclassify the document as a guideline so business units can deviate when the named product is unsuitable
Rewrite the document as a procedure giving step-by-step instructions for deploying the encryption product

q: A business impact analysis concludes that the order-management database can tolerate the loss of no more than 15 minutes of transactions, yet the platform is currently protected only by a nightly backup. Which continuity metric is unmet, and what change does it drive?
c: The recovery time objective, requiring faster restoration procedures at the alternate site
The maximum tolerable downtime, requiring a shorter overall outage window
The recovery point objective, requiring near-continuous replication or transaction journaling
The mean time between failures, requiring more reliable database server hardware

q: While developing the business continuity plan for a chemical processing facility, the planning team debates what the plan's highest priority must be if a disaster strikes during working hours. Which priority MUST come first?
c: Protecting the lives and safety of personnel and the surrounding community
Preserving the integrity of financial and operational data
Restoring revenue-generating production as quickly as possible
Meeting regulatory incident-reporting deadlines for the event

q: A regional bank periodically moves employees among accounts-payable, reconciliation, and vendor-onboarding positions. Shortly after one such move, the incoming employee uncovers a long-running invoice fraud arranged by the previous holder of the role. Which personnel security practice enabled this discovery?
c: Separation of duties
Mandatory vacations
Job rotation
Dual control

q: A senior engineer with deep knowledge of proprietary algorithms resigns to join a direct competitor. Management is concerned about disclosure of trade secrets after the departure. Which offboarding measure BEST protects the organization while remaining legally defensible?
c: Withhold the final paycheck until the engineer signs a new, broader noncompete agreement
Hold an exit interview that reviews the engineer's continuing NDA obligations and confirms return of all assets and credentials
Send the competitor formal notice that the engineer possesses the organization's trade secrets
Retain the engineer's system accounts in an active state so activity can be monitored after the departure date

q: A development team has finished enumerating threats against a new application and now needs a simple, repeatable scheme to rate each one, considering factors such as potential damage, reproducibility, exploitability, affected users, and discoverability, so the worst threats are fixed first. Which approach fits this need?
c: PASTA
CVSS
VAST
DREAD

q: A security analyst places the adversary objective 'exfiltrate the customer database' at the top of a diagram, then decomposes it into alternative branches of sub-goals connected by AND/OR logic, assigning feasibility and cost estimates to each leaf node to find the cheapest viable path. Which threat modeling technique is this?
c: Data flow diagram decomposition
Cyber kill chain mapping
Attack tree analysis
Misuse case modeling

q: A critical SaaS vendor satisfies every security term in its contract, but a breach occurs at a hosting subcontractor the vendor engaged without the customer's knowledge, and the customer finds it has no contractual recourse. Which contract change would BEST prevent a recurrence of this blind spot?
c: Prohibit the vendor from engaging any subcontractors or third parties in delivering the contracted service
Increase the organization's cyber insurance coverage for losses arising from incidents at the vendor
Require the vendor to submit the results of its own annual penetration tests for customer review
Require security obligations to flow down to all subcontractors, with advance disclosure and approval of subprocessors

q: An organization's security education effort consists of one generic annual module taken by all staff. Developers continue to introduce injection flaws into applications, and service-desk agents keep resetting passwords for callers without verifying identity. What is the BEST improvement to the program?
c: Deliver the same awareness module quarterly instead of annually to increase repetition
Apply disciplinary consequences to employees who fail security assessments
Add role-based training that targets the specific risks and duties of each job function
Replace the training program with stronger preventive technical controls

q: A CISSP-credentialed consultant is engaged to produce an independent comparison of three security products and then realizes she holds a substantial equity stake in one of the vendors. Under the ISC2 Code of Ethics, what is the BEST course of action?
c: Disclose the financial interest to the client and offer to withdraw from the engagement
Proceed with the evaluation while making a deliberate personal effort to remain objective
Quietly sell the equity stake and then continue the engagement without informing the client
Complete the comparison but silently exclude the vendor in which she holds equity

q: During a study group session, a CISSP-certified colleague distributes a document containing what he says are actual questions memorized from his recent ISC2 exam sitting. Another certified member asks him to stop; he refuses and continues sharing the file. Which action by the certified member BEST upholds the ISC2 Code of Ethics?
c: Quietly leave the study group so he is not personally associated with the leaked material
Report the colleague's conduct to the colleague's employer so HR can discipline him
File an ethics complaint with ISC2 reporting the breach of the examination agreement
Take no further action, since asking the colleague to stop already fulfilled his ethical duty

q: After a ransomware infection encrypts a file server, the operations team rebuilds the server and restores its data from the previous night's backups, returning the business to normal operation. Which control category do the rebuild and restore activities BEST represent?
c: Detective
Corrective
Preventive
Compensating

q: A company's CISO reports to the CIO, whose annual bonus is tied to on-time project delivery and IT cost reduction. Security findings that would delay projects are repeatedly downgraded or removed before reaching executive leadership. From a governance perspective, which action BEST addresses the root cause of this problem?
c: Require the CISO to present quarterly security metrics to the CIO's leadership team
Increase the security budget so findings can be remediated without delaying project schedules
Adopt a formal risk scoring methodology so that findings are rated consistently and objectively
Move the CISO's reporting line outside the CIO's organization, such as to the CEO or a board risk committee

q: A retail startup's founder insists the company need not follow PCI DSS because no statute in their country requires it. The company accepts credit card payments through a major card brand via an acquiring bank. Which statement MOST accurately characterizes the company's obligation?
c: It is a contractual obligation flowing from agreements with the card brands and acquiring bank, and violations can bring fines or loss of card processing
It is an international treaty ratified by most nations, so it already carries the force of law regardless of any local statute
It is voluntary guidance similar to a guideline, so the company may adopt only the controls it finds convenient or affordable
It applies only to issuing banks and payment processors, so merchants that merely accept cards fall outside its scope

q: An investigator seizes a laptop that may become evidence in a court case. Which practice is MOST important for demonstrating that the evidence was not altered while in the organization's possession, so that it remains admissible?
c: Encrypting the laptop's drive so its contents cannot be modified by anyone
Building a timeline of the suspected attacker's actions from available log data
Maintaining a documented chain of custody recording every handler, transfer, and storage location
Interviewing the laptop's assigned user before any forensic imaging takes place

q: A financial services firm acquires a fintech subsidiary and simultaneously becomes subject to a new consumer privacy regulation. Its information security policy was last reviewed 10 months ago on an annual cycle, with the next review due in 2 months. What is the BEST course of action for the security policy?
c: Wait for the scheduled review so all changes are made at once and the policy remains stable
Begin an immediate out-of-cycle policy review to address the acquisition and the new regulation
Publish a new procedure covering the regulation's requirements and leave the policy itself unchanged
Let the subsidiary continue operating under its own legacy security policy until the next annual review

q: A payment-processing application has a maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) of 8 hours. The recovery team can restore the system's infrastructure in 5 hours, but validating restored data, reprocessing queued transactions, and confirming users can resume work takes an additional 4 hours. Which conclusion should the business continuity planner draw?
c: The strategy is inadequate because restoration plus work recovery time totals 9 hours, exceeding the MTD
The strategy is adequate because the 5-hour technical restoration finishes well within the 8-hour MTD
The MTD should be raised to 9 hours so that the documented recovery strategy remains compliant
The 4 hours of validation counts against the RPO, which addresses acceptable data loss rather than downtime

q: An employee hired 6 years ago as a help desk technician, with only a basic background check at hire, is being promoted to a role administering the company's wire transfer platform. Which personnel security practice is MOST appropriate before granting the new access?
c: Rely on the original background check, since it returned no adverse findings when she was hired
Have the employee sign a stronger nondisclosure agreement that covers financial transaction data
Assign a manager to directly supervise all of the employee's activities during her first year in the role
Conduct a new screening, including financial and criminal checks, proportionate to the new role's sensitivity

q: A risk analyst evaluates safeguards for a system with an annualized loss expectancy (ALE) of $120,000. Option A costs $30,000 per year and reduces ALE to $40,000. Option B costs $10,000 per year and reduces ALE to $90,000. Option C costs $55,000 per year and reduces ALE to $20,000. Using cost-benefit analysis, which choice provides the GREATEST net benefit?
c: Option B, because it imposes the lowest annual safeguard cost on the budget
Option C, because it drives the residual ALE down to the lowest possible level
Option A, because its ALE reduction minus its annual cost gives the greatest net value
Options A and C combined, because layering both safeguards maximizes total risk reduction

q: A development team is planning a new customer-facing application. The security architect wants threat modeling to deliver the most value at the lowest remediation cost. When should the FIRST threat modeling session occur?
c: After penetration testing, so the model can be validated against real exploit findings
During design, before code is written, so identified threats can shape the architecture
Immediately after deployment, once the true production configuration is finally known
During code review, when concrete implementation details are available for examination

q: A hospital licenses a critical patient-scheduling application from a small software vendor with uncertain financial stability. The hospital's chief concern is losing the ability to maintain the application if the vendor goes out of business. Which contractual measure BEST addresses this specific supply chain risk?
c: A source code escrow agreement that releases the code to the hospital upon defined vendor-failure events
A service level agreement imposing financial penalties whenever uptime commitments are missed
A right-to-audit clause permitting annual reviews of the vendor's security control environment
A nondisclosure agreement protecting the patient information the hospital shares with the vendor

q: A security awareness program launched 3 years ago still uses its original modules. Recently, employees were targeted by AI-generated voice phishing calls impersonating executives, a technique the program never mentions, and several complied with fraudulent payment instructions. What is the BEST improvement to the program?
c: Discipline the employees who complied with the fraudulent calls to reinforce accountability
Deliver the existing training modules quarterly instead of annually to increase repetition
Replace the awareness sessions with a technical control that screens inbound external calls
Establish a recurring content review so the program covers current techniques such as deepfake vishing

q: An accounts payable clerk is able to create new vendor records in the finance system and also approve payments to those vendors. An audit finds the clerk created a fictitious vendor and paid it for months. Which security principle was violated, enabling this fraud?
c: Least privilege
Need to know
Separation of duties
Defense in depth

q: A departing developer reimplements, from memory and public documentation, the same scheduling algorithm used in his former employer's product, writing entirely new source code for a competitor. The former employer sues for copyright infringement. Why is the copyright claim MOST likely to fail?
c: Copyright protects the particular expression of source code, not the underlying algorithm or idea
Copyright in software expires 10 years after first publication, and that period has elapsed
Copyright does not extend to software at all, which can be protected only through patents
Copyright was forfeited because the employer never registered the program with a government office

q: HR asks the security team to investigate whether an employee violated the acceptable use policy by running a personal business from a company laptop. Leadership intends, at most, to terminate the employee, and no regulator or law enforcement referral is anticipated. Which statement BEST describes how this investigation should be conducted?
c: It must satisfy the beyond-a-reasonable-doubt standard because the employee's livelihood is at stake
It is an administrative investigation with a low burden of proof, but evidence should still be handled soundly in case the matter later escalates
It requires a court-issued search warrant before any company-owned laptop may be examined
It must be conducted under attorney-client privilege because internal investigations always require outside counsel

q: A risk manager wants senior stakeholders to estimate the likelihood and impact of several strategic risks, but past workshops were dominated by the most senior executive in the room, and other participants simply agreed with her views. Which technique BEST counteracts this problem?
c: A Monte Carlo simulation that replaces stakeholder judgment with statistical modeling
A facilitated brainstorming workshop with every stakeholder present in the same room
A series of one-on-one interviews conducted solely with the most senior executive
The Delphi technique, collecting anonymous estimates through iterative feedback rounds

q: A dispute arises over who should set the classification level of a newly created customer analytics dataset. The database administrator claims the decision is hers because she manages the platform; the security team argues it should classify all data centrally. Under security governance principles, who SHOULD make this decision?
c: The business executive accountable for the dataset, acting in the role of data owner
The database administrator, because custodians manage the platform where the data resides
The security team, because assigning classifications is inherently a security function
The end users of the dataset, because they understand best how the data will be used

q: During a business impact analysis, order fulfillment is rated the company's most time-critical process and its ERP system is given a 4-hour recovery objective. In a later disaster, fulfillment cannot resume for 2 days because an internally hosted label-printing service and a courier-integration gateway had no recovery provisions. Which BIA activity was performed inadequately?
c: Assigning maximum tolerable downtime values to the business processes
Calculating the annualized loss expectancy for the ERP platform
Identifying the supporting resources and dependencies each critical process relies on
Selecting an alternate processing site with enough capacity for the ERP system

q: After implementing multifactor authentication, centralized logging, and hardened configurations for its remote access service, an organization determines that some exposure to credential phishing remains despite these controls. Which term describes this remaining exposure, and what should be done with it?
c: Inherent risk; it should be recalculated assuming that no controls are in place
Residual risk; it should be weighed against the risk appetite and formally accepted or further treated
Secondary risk; it is a brand-new risk introduced by the risk responses themselves
Total risk; it is the full exposure that exists before any safeguards are applied

q: A CISSP consultant completes a security assessment for a client. Before the report goes to the client's board, the CIO who hired the consultant demands that two critical findings be removed, arguing they will be fixed soon anyway, and hints that future contracts depend on cooperation. Which action BEST aligns with the ISC2 Code of Ethics?
c: Remove the findings, because the CIO who engaged the consultant has authority over report content
Send the unedited report directly to the board while concealing the delivery from the CIO
Move the two critical findings into a confidential appendix distributed only to the CIO
Refuse to alter the report, deliver it complete and accurate, and accept possibly losing future work

q: A threat intelligence team wants to map the specific tactics and techniques used by real-world adversary groups known to target its industry, and then check the organization's defensive coverage against each technique. Which resource is BEST suited to this goal?
c: MITRE ATT&CK, a knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques from real-world observation
STRIDE, which sorts threats into six categories such as spoofing and tampering
DREAD, which scores each threat across five factors to rank relative severity
PASTA, a seven-stage risk-centric process for modeling threats against applications

q: A company with 400 suppliers requires every one of them to complete the same 300-question security questionnaire annually. Critical vendors with production data access receive no deeper scrutiny than the office plant service, and the vendor risk team is months behind on reviews. What is the BEST way to restructure the program?
c: Cut the questionnaire to 50 questions so every vendor can be assessed on schedule
Assess only newly onboarded vendors and exempt all existing suppliers from review
Tier vendors by criticality and data access, matching assessment depth to each tier's risk
Require every vendor to carry cyber insurance in place of security assessments

q: A new employee is scheduled to receive access to systems containing trade secrets on her first day. From a personnel security standpoint, which item MUST be completed BEFORE that access is granted?
c: Her first scheduled performance review with her direct manager
Her signed acknowledgment of the NDA and the acceptable use and security policies
Her enrollment in the company's annual security awareness refresher cycle
The completion of her 90-day probationary employment period

q: A European subsidiary must send employee personal data to its parent company's HR system in a country the European Commission has not recognized as providing adequate data protection. The company wants a lawful and practical basis for these routine intra-group transfers to continue. Which mechanism BEST fits this need?
c: Rely on the destination country's domestic privacy laws to protect the data after it arrives
Collect fresh individual consent from every employee before each routine transfer occurs
Encrypt the data in transit, which removes the transfer from the scope of the restrictions
Adopt approved safeguards such as standard contractual clauses or binding corporate rules

q: One year after launch, completion rates for a company's security training remain high, but engagement surveys show employees view security as the security team's job, and business units rarely raise security questions on their own. Which enhancement would BEST help embed security into everyday culture?
c: Create a security champions network of trained volunteer advocates inside each business unit
Make security training completion a formal condition for receiving annual bonus payments
Send more frequent company-wide email bulletins summarizing recent industry breaches
Add more difficult questions to the training quizzes to raise the required passing score

q: A middleware team requests that a new application service account be added to the domain administrators group "so we never hit permission errors during deployments." Granting this request would MOST directly violate which security principle?
c: Need to know, because the account could read data unrelated to its function
Separation of duties, because one account would combine deployment and administrative work
Least privilege, because the account would hold far more rights than its tasks require
Defense in depth, because a single control layer would protect all administrative functions

q: To reduce the risk of social engineering, an organization implements a mandatory annual security awareness course, a signed acceptable use agreement, and a documented sanctions process for violations. These measures are BEST classified as which category of control?
c: Administrative controls
Technical controls
Physical controls
Compensating controls

q: A CISSP-certified consultant who specializes in enterprise network security is offered a lucrative engagement to lead a safety-critical assessment of an industrial control system environment, a field in which she has no training or experience. Under the ISC2 Code of Ethics, which is the BEST course of action?
c: Accept the engagement and quietly study industrial control fundamentals as the work proceeds
Disclose her lack of industrial control expertise to the client and either decline or engage qualified specialists
Accept the engagement only if the client signs a liability waiver acknowledging the risk
Report the client to ISC2 for offering her work outside the scope of her certification

q: During pre-launch legal review of a commercial software product, counsel discovers that developers embedded a library distributed under a strong copyleft open-source license (such as the GPL) into the company's proprietary application, which is sold to customers. What is the MOST significant legal implication of this finding?
c: Patent infringement, because the library's algorithms may be patented by its original author
Trade secret misappropriation, because the company used code it did not develop itself
Breach of contract requiring retroactive royalty payments for commercial use of the library
License noncompliance that could compel release of the proprietary source code or halt distribution

q: A threat modeling team begins by inventorying the organization's most valuable data and systems, then works outward to analyze how each could be targeted and what the loss would mean. Which threat modeling approach is the team using?
c: An attacker-centric approach that starts from adversary goals and capabilities
An asset-centric approach that starts from what the organization values most
A software-centric approach that starts from the system's design and components
A risk-centric approach that stages analysis around business impact simulation

q: A business impact analysis ranks processes solely by projected hourly revenue loss. A compliance manager objects that a low-revenue insurance claims process would trigger statutory penalties and serious reputational harm if it were unavailable for two days. What is the BEST way to improve the analysis?
c: Incorporate qualitative criteria such as regulatory penalties and reputational damage into the impact scoring
Re-run the quantitative analysis using more precise revenue figures for every business process
Escalate the disputed processes to the disaster recovery team so it can assign their recovery priorities
Classify the claims process as out of scope because its revenue impact falls below the BIA threshold

q: An analyst must examine a hard drive from a workstation implicated in suspected data theft, and the matter may proceed to litigation. Which practice BEST preserves the evidentiary value of the drive during the examination?
c: Examine the original drive directly so all findings are drawn from the primary evidence
Photograph the drive and record its serial number, then return the workstation to service
Create a bit-for-bit image verified with matching cryptographic hashes and analyze only the copy
Copy the relevant user files to an analysis server using the operating system's file explorer

q: Employees across the company have begun pasting proprietary source code and customer records into public generative AI chatbots. The CISO wants a governance document that states management's mandatory rules on acceptable and prohibited uses of such tools for the entire workforce. Which document type is MOST appropriate?
c: A system-specific policy governing the configuration of one approved AI platform
A guideline offering recommended practices for responsible AI experimentation
A baseline defining the minimum technical settings for AI-enabled endpoints
An issue-specific security policy stating management's rules for generative AI use

q: An organization repeatedly discovers after contracts are signed that newly selected SaaS vendors cannot meet its encryption and breach notification expectations, forcing costly amendments and rework. Which action BEST addresses the root cause?
c: Add a right-to-audit clause to each existing vendor contract at its next renewal
Define mandatory security requirements in the RFP and evaluate candidate vendors against them before selection
Require every prospective vendor to carry cyber liability insurance before onboarding
Transfer responsibility for vendor oversight from procurement to the security operations center

q: The board of directors asks the CISO for quarterly reporting on the security program. Previous presentations listed thousands of blocked intrusion attempts and patch counts, and directors said they could not use the information to make decisions. Which reporting approach is MOST useful at board level?
c: Present business-aligned metrics showing risk trends, control effectiveness, and progress against strategic objectives
Provide the complete vulnerability scan reports so directors can review the technical detail themselves
Report only that the organization remained compliant with all applicable regulations during the quarter
Increase the reporting frequency to monthly so directors receive operational counts sooner

q: An organization outsources after-hours support to a firm whose technicians receive privileged access to customer databases. Internal staff in comparable roles must pass background checks under the personnel security policy, but nothing equivalent applies to the outsourcer. What is the BEST way to address the personnel risk posed by the vendor's technicians?
c: Require the vendor to sign a general nondisclosure agreement covering its entire workforce
Accept the risk, because the vendor's employees fall outside the organization's direct authority
Contractually require the vendor to screen its personnel to a standard commensurate with internal requirements and provide evidence of compliance
Rely on session monitoring of the technicians' activity in place of any screening requirement

q: Five percent of the workforce repeatedly fails phishing simulations despite completing the annual awareness course. An operations manager proposes publicly naming repeat clickers and terminating anyone who fails three times. From an awareness program perspective, what is the BEST response to the repeat-clicker problem?
c: Adopt the proposal, because visible consequences deter risky behavior across the workforce
Exempt repeat clickers from future simulations to avoid embarrassing them further
Replace the simulations with a longer annual computer-based training course for all employees
Deliver targeted remedial training and coaching to repeat clickers and measure whether their behavior improves

q: Attackers compromise a company's chronically unpatched servers and use them to launch a denial-of-service attack against a business partner, causing the partner substantial losses. The partner sues, arguing the company failed to maintain reasonable security on systems that were then used to harm others. Which legal concept is the partner's claim based on?
c: Vicarious liability for the acts committed by the attackers
Downstream liability arising from negligence in securing its own systems
Strict liability, because harm occurred regardless of the precautions taken
Contributory negligence by the partner for failing to block the attack traffic

q: A project team finishes deploying a data loss prevention platform that was the approved treatment for a high-rated data exfiltration risk. The project manager asks the risk manager to mark the risk register entry closed because the project completed on schedule. What should the risk manager do FIRST?
c: Assess whether the control operates effectively and update the residual risk before changing the entry's status
Close the entry, since the approved treatment plan was fully executed
Transfer the entry to the internal audit team's follow-up log for review at the next annual audit
Reclassify the risk as accepted, because a mitigating control is now in place

q: A developer argues that an internal reporting portal needs no authentication because its URL is long, randomly generated, "impossible to guess," and not linked from anywhere. This reasoning is BEST described as reliance on what?
c: Defense in depth, because the hidden URL adds an extra protective layer
Least privilege, because only staff who know the URL can reach the portal
Security through obscurity, because protection depends entirely on keeping a design detail secret
Open design, because the portal's protection has been openly evaluated by the team

q: A national banking authority formally notifies a bank that it is examining the bank's compliance with cybersecurity provisions of banking rules, demands production of records, and warns that failure to cooperate can result in fines or license actions. Which type of investigation is this?
c: A criminal investigation, requiring proof beyond a reasonable doubt
A civil investigation initiated by a harmed private party seeking damages
An administrative investigation conducted internally under company policy
A regulatory investigation conducted by a government agency with power to compel compliance

q: An enterprise with two hundred agile development teams needs threat modeling that plugs into sprint workflows, scales across the entire application portfolio through automation, and produces output usable by developers and operations staff without embedding a security expert in every team. Which methodology was designed for this need?
c: PASTA, which works through seven stages aligning attack simulation with business impact analysis
VAST, which uses visual process and application models designed to scale across agile teams through automation
STRIDE, which enumerates six threat categories against each element of a system model
DREAD, which scores each identified threat across five standardized rating factors

q: During a surprise continuity exercise, the call tree references employees who left months ago, the designated alternate work area was closed in a real-estate consolidation, and a critical application migrated to SaaS eighteen months ago appears nowhere in the plan. What is the BEST way to prevent this situation from recurring?
c: Schedule a comprehensive rewrite of the continuity plan every five years
Assign ownership of the plan to internal audit so errors are caught during annual audits
Integrate plan updates into change management and personnel processes so triggering events prompt revisions
Store the plan in a document portal that timestamps and logs every download

q: A CISSP-credentialed researcher independently discovers a remotely exploitable flaw in infusion pump software deployed in hospitals worldwide. No patch exists. Which course of action is MOST consistent with the ISC2 Code of Ethics?
c: Privately notify the vendor with details, allow reasonable time to remediate, and involve a coordination body if the vendor is unresponsive
Publish complete technical details immediately so hospitals and the public can defend themselves without delay
Keep the finding confidential indefinitely so that the details can never reach potential attackers
Offer the technical details to the vendor in exchange for a consulting fee, since competent work merits compensation

q: A new CISO inherits a ninety-page "security policy" that mixes statements of management intent with firewall vendor commands, server hardening parameters, and help-desk scripts. Because any product upgrade forces full re-approval by the executive committee, the document is chronically outdated and widely ignored. What is the BEST structural remedy?
c: Delegate approval authority for the document to the network engineering team to speed up updates
Convert the entire document into a guideline so future updates no longer require approval
Require the executive committee to meet monthly so re-approvals keep pace with technology change
Separate the content into a concise technology-neutral policy with subordinate standards and procedures on faster review cycles

q: A critical payments vendor passed the organization's onboarding security assessment two years ago. The organization learns from news reports that the vendor suffered a major breach four months earlier and was recently acquired by a foreign investment firm; its next annual questionnaire is not due for five months. Which program improvement BEST addresses the weakness this reveals?
c: Expand the annual questionnaire to cover additional security control domains
Require ISO/IEC 27001 certification from all critical vendors at onboarding
Add continuous monitoring and contractual notification obligations for material events between assessments
Screen out vendor candidates that appear likely to be acquired during the contract term

q: A storage administrator configures backups, applies retention settings, and restores files for the finance department's records, following protection requirements that the finance director has defined. The administrator's role with respect to this data is BEST described as which of the following?
c: Data owner, because he exercises hands-on control over the data every day
Data custodian, because he implements protections on behalf of the owner
Data processor, because he handles personal data as defined in privacy law
Data steward, because he ensures the data's quality and business meaning

q: An internal audit finds that a specialist who transferred from payroll to procurement three years ago can still run payroll and can now also approve purchase orders, a combination that has existed unnoticed since the transfer. Which personnel security practice MOST directly prevents this condition?
c: Requiring access reviews and revalidation of entitlements whenever an employee changes roles
Conducting exit interviews with all employees who leave the organization
Enforcing mandatory vacations so a substitute periodically performs each employee's duties
Rescreening employees before they are promoted into positions of higher sensitivity

q: A product team designing a newsletter signup form proposes also collecting each subscriber's birth date, employer, and income range because "the data might be useful for future campaigns." The company operates under a comprehensive privacy statute modeled on the GDPR. This proposal MOST directly conflicts with which privacy principle?
c: Storage limitation, because the marketing records would be retained longer than necessary
Data sovereignty, because the additional fields might be replicated to servers in other countries
Accuracy, because self-reported income ranges are likely to be unreliable
Data minimization, because personal data collected must be limited to what the stated purpose requires

q: An awareness team compares two program designs. Design A is a forty-five-minute course delivered once each January. Design B pairs a short annual module with brief lessons displayed the instant an employee clicks a simulated phishing link or is blocked attempting to email a sensitive file externally. Which learning principle BEST explains why Design B is more likely to reduce risky behavior?
c: Massed practice, because one concentrated comprehensive session builds deeper retention
Deterrence, because employees behave more carefully when they know their actions are watched
Reinforcement at the moment of error, because immediate feedback in context changes behavior more than delayed generic instruction
Gamification, because turning the simulations into a competition motivates participation
